Tap the Scan QR Code button to open the camera with a square viewfinder. Point the QR code into the frame — the result is sent to Google Sheets or saved locally.\n\nLong-press the Scan button to open the gallery and pick an image containing a QR code from device storage.
Type an ID or Name in the text field and tap the Send button to submit it without scanning.

Every scan is automatically numbered — Scan #1, Scan #2, and so on. The number is shown in the Last Scan section on the main screen. To reset the numbering back to 0, open Settings and tap Reset Scan Number.
When Local Storage is enabled, data is saved on the device. Open Local Data to view all saved records.
Set the Apps Script URL, sheet name, data storage, scan number reset, and dark mode view.
[a] Go to sheets.google.com and create the spreadsheet which has timestamp at column A and ID at column B at headers row 1. [b] Share it in which anyone with the link can edit.
In Google Sheet, click Extensions → Apps Script. This opens the script editor bound to your spreadsheet.
Get script at https://s.id/gappscr and paste it in script editor. Save the project (Ctrl+S).
Click Deploy → New deployment. Choose Web App. Set \'Execute as\' to yourself and \'Who has access\' to Anyone. Click Deploy and authorise the app when prompted.
Step 5 — Copy the Web App URL
Copy the Web App URL (starts with https://script.google.com/macros/). Paste it into the Settings screen of Attendly along with the target sheet tab name.

Attendly is a lightweight QR-code attendance tracker. Scan QR codes or enter IDs manually to record attendance directly into a Google Sheet or store records locally for bulk upload later.

• QR code scanning via camera or local file
• Manual ID entry
• Direct Google Sheets integration via Apps Script
• Offline / local storage mode
• Bulk upload from local records
• Configurable sheet name
